items.title: Establishment of the engineering centre
items.text: Russian Railways (RZD) and the Sinara group of companies incorporated the Railway Transport Engineering Centre.
items.imageAlt: Signing of RZD-Sinara joint engineering agreement.

items.title: Domestic high-speed rolling stock programme
items.text: Launch of domestic high-speed train development programme.

items.title: Infrastructure development centre established
items.text: A new infrastructure development track opened; catenary and permanent-way programmes commenced.
items.imageAlt: Catenary systems and permanent-way development projects.

items.title: Forward-looking projects centre established
items.text: A new innovative rolling-stock development track opened. Hydrogen and hybrid locomotive programmes launched.

items.title: ECRT trials at the VNIIZHT Experimental Ring
items.text: Endurance trials began on ECRT-developed permanent-way engineered for an accumulated gross tonnage of 2.5 billion tonnes, on the VNIIZHT Experimental Ring.

items.title: High-speed train technical design completed
items.text: Core technical solutions were developed for Russia’s first domestic high-speed electric train.

items.title: ECRT trials on the RZD network
items.text: Field trials began on ECRT-developed permanent-way engineered for an accumulated gross tonnage of 2.5 billion tonnes — on a section of the Krasnoyarsk Railway, an RZD branch.

items.title: Working design completed and high-speed train production started
items.text: Engineering documentation for Russia’s first domestic high-speed electric train was completed; carbody fabrication started at the Ural Locomotives plant.

future.title: Russia’s train of the future
future.lead: The high-speed electric train is manufactured at the Ural Locomotives plant. The engineering solutions developed by ECRT match world-class benchmarks and, for several subsystems, exceed them. Planned launch year is 2028.
future.videoAria: Night-time animation of a high-speed train in an urban skyline.

flagship.sectionTitle:
First VSM line
Moscow – Saint Petersburg
flagship.description: We deliver the core technical solutions for the first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg: rolling stock, catenary, and rail fastening.
flagship.mapAlt: Infographic of the first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg route: stations and design-speed segments.

facts.title: Stations on the route
facts.body: The first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg will have 14 stopping points.

facts.title: Line length
facts.body: New track on a concrete subgrade in sections in Moscow and Saint Petersburg.

facts.title: Train readiness
facts.body: A total of 43 high-speed electric trains will be delivered in 2030.

projects.title: Main projects
projects.evsHomeShowcaseDescription: Development of rolling stock for the first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg. ECRT prepares the specification and conceptual, technical, and detailed design documentation; manufacturing takes place at the Ural Locomotives plant (part of the Sinara Transport Machines group).
projects.showcaseEvsTitle: Russia’s first domestic high-speed electric train
projects.showcaseKs400ModelDescription: The catenary mathematical model enables finite-element calculations of static catenary performance and of dynamic interaction between the catenary and electric rolling stock pantographs.
projects.showcaseContactVsm1Description: The KS-400 catenary product range ensures reliable power transfer to train pantographs at speeds up to 400 km/h.
projects.showcaseVsm1TrackDescription: ECRT is developing rail fastenings for railway track on a ballastless subgrade for the first VSM line Moscow – Saint Petersburg
projects.showcaseTrackV25Title: Innovative railway track structure for heavily loaded sections and its elements (Path V2.5)
projects.showcaseOperationSupportTitle: Operations support - Sapsan and Lastochka EMUs
showcaseOperationSupportDescriptions: Support for operation of German-built Sapsan high-speed EMUs and ES1 Lastochka regional electric trains.
The project includes engineering support for structural changes to Sapsan and Lastochka trains as part of import substitution and to improve passenger comfort.
